data.title: Bitcoin price nears pivotal support: here’s why it may drop by 38% soon
data.description:
Bitcoin price extended its downward trend for the seventh consecutive week as demand from investors waned. BTC tumbled to $61.584, and technicals suggest that it may drop further in the coming weeks as ETF outflows rise and futures open interest drops.

Bitcoin price continues falling as ETF outflows rise

One of the key reasons why Bitcoin price may continue falling is that American investors have continued selling their ETFs this month. ETFs shed over $582 million on Thursday, bringing the monthly outflows to over $3.47 billion. These outflows follow the $515 million that were lost last month. 

Before that, Bitcoin ETFs added over $2.6 billion in assets in September and $3.52 billion in August this year. The outflows have coincided with the ongoing retreat of Bitcoin’s futures open interest, which has dropped to $45 billion from the year-to-date high of over $60 billion.

Bitcoin has dropped for several reasons. The most notable is the $6.3 billion Binance hack, which has been linked to North Korea. Binance and its partners managed to freeze $3 billion of the stolen funds. 

Although Binance has covered the losses, the incident has severely damaged investor confidence. Binance is also one of the most respected crypto exchanges in the world, so if it can be hacked, there is a fear that no exchange is safe.

Bitcoin has also fallen because of the midterm elections, in which Democrats made big gains. They now hold 56 seats in the Senate and a larger margin in the House of Representatives. As a result, the crypto market is bracing for more scrutiny, investigations, and regulation. 

In theory, tighter rules should be bullish for the industry because they would help keep out bad actors. Notably, Bitcoin and altcoins underperformed during the first two years of Trump’s presidency.

Rising US bond yields and geopolitical tensions

Bitcoin price has slumped as investors react to the ongoing performance in the bond market. Data shows that the short and long term US bond yields have continued rising this month. The benchmark 10-year yield has jumped to 5.1%, while the five-year has continued soaring. 

These yields jumped because of the recent macro data. Numbers showed that the unemployment rate dropped to 4.1%, while the economy created over 165k jobs. US inflation has also remained stubbornly high in the past few months.

These metrics suggest that the Federal Reserve will hike interest rates, putting pressure on risky assets like Bitcoin and stocks. 

Further, there are signs that geopolitical tensions between the US and Iran are escalating. The latest reporting suggests that Trump is considering launching attacks against key Iranian targets, a move that will lead to an escalation. Iran is also working to block the blockade, with the IRGC warning that it will strike Gulf energy infrastructure if the US attacks its ships.

Therefore, there is a risk that crude oil prices will continue rising, leading to higher inflation and interest rates.

Bitcoin price technical analysis

BTC price chart | Source: TradingView

Technicals suggests that Bitcoin is at risk of a big drop in the near term. It initially dropped to the 61.8% Fibonacci Retracement level of $57,753 in July and then bounced back. Those gains were limited as the coin faced substantial resistance at $87,500. 

Now, the coin is attempting to retest the key support level of $57,753. It has also crossed the 50-week and 200-week Exponential Moving Averages (EMA). Therefore, there is a risk that Bitcoin will continue falling in the near term. The next key target to watch will be the 78.6% retracement level at $38,866, which is down by 37% below the current level.

data.title: Eight years: From a crypto exchange to a global ecosystem serving 40 million users
data.description:
What started eight years ago as a cryptocurrency exchange has evolved into an international business ecosystem of 11 companies serving approximately 40 million users worldwide.

As WhiteBIT celebrates its eighth anniversary and W Group marks its first year, the milestones highlight a transformation from a single trading platform into a diversified business connecting traditional finance, digital assets and emerging technologies.

The scale of this growth is reflected in WhiteBIT's $2.8 trillion trading volume in 2026 and more than 5,500 institutional clients.

Meanwhile, W Group has expanded from eight to 11 companies in one year, growing its combined user base from 35 million to approximately 40 million.

From one exchange to a global business ecosystem

Established in 2025, W Group brought together businesses developed around WhiteBIT under a broader strategy: connecting traditional finance and digital assets while extending their applications into new industries.

The group aims to build more than a portfolio of independent companies.

By combining financial infrastructure, technology and expertise, its businesses can develop new services, reach new markets and create opportunities across industries.

In 2026, W Group expanded well beyond financial services. Dutch sports car manufacturer Spyker joined the group in June, opening opportunities to apply digital finance and blockchain technology to luxury automotive.

W Group has also made a $400 million investment commitment in SignSplit, the signed-data platform for the AI era. The seed round values SignSplit at $1 billion.

In banking, Georgia-based hashbank, a fully licensed digital bank, combines traditional banking services with cryptocurrency functionality, allowing customers to manage fiat and digital assets within one environment.

Together, these businesses illustrate W Group's strategy of connecting financial services, technology and consumer-facing products into an ecosystem where each company can contribute to the growth of the others.

WhiteBIT at Eight: Expanding Global Trading

WhiteBIT remains a central pillar of W Group, providing trading infrastructure and digital asset services for retail and institutional clients.

In 2026, the exchange recorded $2.8 trillion in trading volume, with derivatives generating approximately $3.5 billion in daily activity. Its platform now offers nearly 1,200 trading markets.

Trading conditions have also improved. Spot trading volume across WhiteBIT's flagship BTC, ETH and WBT pairs increased more than fivefold, from $53 billion in 2020 to $276 billion in 2025.

Meanwhile, bid-ask spreads across its major markets have narrowed approximately threefold since 2021, reflecting deeper liquidity.

WhiteBIT also serves more than 5,500 institutional clients, including funds, brokers and payment providers, through over 20 dedicated products and services.

Businesses can access crypto liquidity, manage digital asset transactions and move between fiat currencies and cryptocurrencies through a single platform.

A landmark year for regulatory expansion

WhiteBIT's eighth year brought significant regulatory milestones that strengthen the group's international presence.

In June 2026, WhiteBIT EU secured authorisation under the EU's Markets in Crypto-Assets Regulation (MiCA) from Austria's Financial Market Authority, establishing a regulatory foundation for providing crypto-asset services across the European Union.

In May, WhiteBIT launched a dedicated platform for users in the United Kingdom, expanding into another major financial market with demanding regulatory requirements.

The company also joined Ghana's regulatory sandbox in March, contributing to the development of the country's digital asset regulatory framework.

These developments reflect WhiteBIT's investment in compliance as a foundation for sustainable international growth.

WBT and a New Blockchain Chapter

The growth of the ecosystem is also reflected in WBT, WhiteBIT's native coin, which reached an all-time high of nearly $88 in September 2026, up from its launch price of $1.62 in 2022.*

The milestone reflects WBT's strong long-term performance alongside the expansion of WhiteBIT and its ecosystem.

WBT's role is also expanding beyond trading. In November, Whitechain transitioned into an Ethereum Layer 2 network built on the OP Stack in partnership with Optimism, with WBT used to pay transaction fees.

Designed to support blockchain applications and financial services, Whitechain has already attracted interest from developers, with more than 140 teams applying to its Builders Program ahead of the network's public launch planned for later in November.

Building the next generation of financial services

For W Group, the next stage of growth will focus on connecting its businesses more closely and turning their combined capabilities into new products and services.

"Eight years ago, we started with one cryptocurrency exchange. Today, we've grown into an international group of 11 companies serving around 40 million users. But our ambition has never been simply to build more businesses. We want to connect them in ways that create real value — bringing traditional finance and digital assets closer together, making new technologies more accessible and opening opportunities across industries," said Volodymyr Nosov, Founder and President of W Group.

Looking ahead, W Group aims to strengthen its presence in regulated markets, expand institutional financial services and accelerate blockchain infrastructure development.

Its long-term vision is an interconnected ecosystem where banking, payments, digital assets and emerging technologies work together, making financial services more accessible to people and businesses worldwide.

data.title: Ethereum price falls below $1,800: is a bigger crash coming?
data.description:
Ethereum (ETH) struggled to maintain its recovery on Friday, down 3.5% in the last 24 hours and now trading below $1,800.

This bearish performance comes as declining stablecoin reserves, expectations of further Federal Reserve interest rate hikes, and weakness in US equities weighed on investor sentiment.

The second-largest cryptocurrency briefly climbed above $1,800 on Thursday but reversed course over the last few hours. 

The decline coincided with a broader sell-off in technology stocks despite a record initial public offering from artificial intelligence company Anthropic.

Meanwhile, on-chain data from Nansen suggests that liquidity is leaving the cryptocurrency market, with stablecoin supply falling by approximately $16 billion over the past month.

Ethereum's technical outlook also remains weak, although oversold momentum indicators suggest that a temporary rebound is possible.

Ethereum dips below $1,800 as Anthropic IPO fails to lift market sentiment

ETH briefly moved above $1,800 on Thursday before reversing its gains as trading activity increased over the last 24 hours. 

The sell-off occurred despite a record initial public offering from artificial intelligence company Anthropic. Anthropic debuted on the Nasdaq at $111.50 per share, approximately 34% above its IPO price of $83, before ending the day trading around $97. 

For Ethereum and the broader cryptocurrency market, weakness in technology stocks can contribute to declining risk appetite.

Stablecoin supply drops $16 billion as crypto market liquidity weakens

Declining stablecoin reserves represent another challenge for Ethereum's recovery. According to on-chain analytics platform Nansen, the total supply of stablecoins across the cryptocurrency market has fallen by approximately $16 billion over the past month.

The decline has reduced the market's stablecoin supply to around $286 billion. Ethereum accounts for approximately $12 billion of the reduction, with increased redemptions involving Tether's USDT and Circle's USDC.

A sustained decline in stablecoin supply can indicate that capital is leaving the digital asset ecosystem rather than simply moving between cryptocurrencies.

Nansen senior research analyst Nicolai Søndergaard suggested that much of the withdrawn capital appears to be moving into traditional cash holdings.

This trend could limit the amount of readily available capital for cryptocurrency purchases.

The outlook for US monetary policy continues to weigh on cryptocurrency sentiment. According to the CME FedWatch Tool figures, the probability of a 25-basis-point interest rate increase at the Federal Reserve's December meeting climbed above 94% on Thursday.

The shift followed the release of minutes from the central bank's October policy meeting, which revealed continued concerns about inflation. Several policymakers indicated that additional monetary tightening could be necessary if inflation remained elevated.

Finally, Ethereum's derivatives market also reflects the pressure facing bullish traders. According to CoinGlass, approximately $104.9 million in ETH positions were liquidated over the previous 24 hours.

Long positions accounted for around $82.9 million of the total, indicating that traders betting on higher prices suffered the larger share of forced closures.

Ethereum remains below major moving averages

Ethereum's daily technical indicators continue to favor sellers. ETH remains below its major Exponential Moving Averages (EMAs), suggesting that the broader downward trend remains intact.

The 20-day EMA stands near $2,017, while the 50-day EMA is positioned around $2,208. Meanwhile, the 100-day EMA sits at approximately $2,255.

All three moving averages remain significantly above Ethereum's current trading range, creating several layers of resistance.

However, momentum indicators suggest that selling pressure may be overstretched. The daily Relative Strength Index stands near 22, placing Ethereum in deeply oversold territory.

Similarly, the Stochastic Oscillator reads approximately 7, indicating that recent price action has been concentrated near the lower end of its trading range.

Ethereum faces several important technical levels as buyers attempt to prevent further losses. The immediate resistance stands at $1,827, a horizontal barrier that has restricted the cryptocurrency's recovery over the past four days.

A sustained breakout above this level could encourage buyers to target the next resistance around $1,971.

Beyond $1,971, Ethereum faces another obstacle near $2,017, where the 20-day EMA is positioned. Further resistance appears around $2,101 and $2,204.

The 50-day EMA near $2,208 and horizontal resistance at $2,250 create an additional supply zone. Higher resistance levels include the 100-day EMA near $2,255 and the previous price pivot around $2,355.

On the downside, Ethereum's possible resistance lies around the psychological 1,770–1,780 region. A sustained breakdown below this area could expose the more significant support level at $1,706.

If buyers fail to defend $1,706, the next downside target stands near $1,603. A deeper correction could eventually bring the $1,512 level into focus.

For now, Ethereum's near-term outlook remains bearish as declining stablecoin reserves, tighter monetary policy expectations, and weak equity market sentiment continue to limit buying demand.

data.title: Why are Samsung and SK Hynix crashing after Nvidia and AMD's sharp losses?
data.description:
Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix stock plunged nearly 6% on Friday as Wall Street's technology sell-off spread to Seoul, deepening investor concerns about the profitability of the artificial intelligence boom.

Samsung fell 6.09% and SK Hynix dropped 5.75% by 11:20 am local time. South Korea's benchmark KOSPI tumbled 4.24% to 4,919.86, surrendering Thursday's recovery.

The declines followed a bruising US session in which Nvidia lost 3.3% and Advanced Micro Devices shed 7.7%.

The scale of the Korean sell-off reflects more than weakness in American chip stocks.

Foreign investors are pulling money out despite strong memory-chip earnings, raising questions about how much investors will pay for future AI growth.

Nvidia, AMD stocks' losses shake confidence in AI

Nvidia's slide came just days after it reported quarterly revenue of $115.8 billion and forecast approximately $130 billion for the following quarter.

The strong numbers confirmed that demand for advanced AI processors remains robust, but failed to settle concerns about expensive data-centre projects and their eventual returns.

AMD faced additional selling after short-seller-linked Hunterbrook Media raised questions about its relationships with Chinese technology companies and potential exposure to US export restrictions.

AMD denied the allegations, which have not been established as violations.

The Nasdaq Composite fell 2.25% on Thursday, while Anthropic's highly anticipated stock-market debut offered little relief.

The AI developer closed 17.1% above its IPO price, but enthusiasm for that listing did not extend across the sector.

Samsung and SK Hynix supply memory used in AI servers, making their shares sensitive to changes in investors' expectations for computing investment.

Aberdeen Investments portfolio manager Isaac Thong described a shift “away from anything linked to AI into anything defensive, high quality and stable,” according to Reuters.

Foreign withdrawals outweigh powerful chip earnings

The pressure is particularly acute in South Korea, where overseas investors have been selling shares for months.

By late Friday morning, foreigners had sold a net 760.54 billion won of KOSPI stocks, while institutions offloaded another 443.61 billion won. Retail investors bought roughly 1.01 trillion won, but could not prevent the decline.

According to Reuters, foreign investors were heading for a seventh consecutive month of net selling, with cumulative withdrawals of approximately $115.2 billion.

That exodus contrasts with record profits at Samsung and SK Hynix, supported by high-bandwidth memory demand and tight production capacity.

Both companies have also announced substantial shareholder-return programmes, although the winding down of some buybacks could weaken an important source of demand for their shares.

Samsung expects memory supplies to remain tight through 2028; SK Hynix has pointed to shortages lasting even longer.

Samsung Futures analyst Jung Hee-chan told MoneyToday that investors need convincing that exceptional chip profits can endure before stronger earnings forecasts translate into higher share prices.

Can battered Korean chip shares recover?

Friday's slide pushed the KOSPI back below 5,000 after Thursday's 1.39% rebound. For traders, reclaiming that threshold would provide an early sign that selling pressure is easing, rather than proof of a lasting recovery.

Thursday's rebound in Samsung and SK Hynix had been supported by local buying, even as overseas investors remained wary.

Friday's retreat suggests bargain hunters alone cannot stabilise the benchmark if international funds continue reducing exposure.

Goldman Sachs has reduced its 12-month KOSPI target to 7,500, though the bank still sees scope for Korean shares to recover from discounted valuations.

Kiwoom Securities analyst Han Ji-young told Seoul Economic Daily that portfolio rotation around Anthropic's IPO could prove short-lived and that bargain hunting might help limit losses.

data.title: Anthropic's ANT closes at $97.17, up 17% on its first day of trading
data.description:
Anthropic’s Class A shares, ticker ANT, closed at $97.17 on their first day on the Nasdaq Global Select Market on 19 November 2026.

That is about 17% above the $83.00 IPO price set a day earlier, and about 13% below the $111.50 opening print.

The day began in Times Square, where co-founders Dario and Daniela Amodei rang the Nasdaq opening bell at 9:30am ET. The ceremony itself did not start trading in ANT. The first trade came later, at 16:50 GMT (11:50am ET), when the shares opened at $111.50, about 34% above the offering price.

Indications had been climbing through the morning, from about $99.60 to $105, then $110 and $111, before the stock opened slightly above that last level. The early burst did not last.

ANT peaked at $115.10 just before noon ET and slipped as low as $92.72.

By mid-afternoon the shares were changing hands around $95.60, still about 15% above the IPO price. The $97.17 close left the debut comfortably above the offering, but well short of the opening pop.

Even so, a 17% first-day gain on the largest IPO on record is a strong debut, the more so on a session in which the main US indexes finished more than 2% lower. The market took some of the opening froth off, but buyers who received stock at $83 still ended the day well in the money.

More than 846 million shares changed hands, ahead of the 522 million traded on SpaceX’s opening day in June, and enough to make ANT the most actively traded name on the Nasdaq. Volume had already passed 640 million by mid-session.

At the $111.50 open, Reuters put Anthropic’s market value at about $2 trillion, a level exceeded by only a handful of US-listed firms, and ahead of the $1.96 trillion it assigned to SpaceX at its June opening trade. That is a reported valuation at the open, not a closing figure.

The fade came as the wider market turned lower. US stocks ended more than 2% down. The Dow Jones Industrial Average lost 1,101.11 points, or 2.19%, to 49,097.06, the S&P 500 fell 2.02% to 7,175.83, and the Nasdaq Composite dropped 2.25% to 23,879.20.

AI shares were mixed as investors weighed worries about higher interest rates. The Nasdaq itself had been up as much as 2% after the open before those gains were given back.

The listing is the first by a frontier AI lab and sets a public-market benchmark for the group, with OpenAI still private. Ordinary investors now have a listed way to take a direct view on a stand-alone model developer, rather than only through the chipmakers and cloud groups that have dominated the trade.

Anthropic sold 980 million Class A shares at $83.00 on Wednesday, of which 956,351,354 were sold by the company and 23,648,646 by selling stockholders. The deal raised about $81.3 billion, making it the largest initial public offering on record, above SpaceX’s initial $75 billion.

The size and price had already been lifted once before the open. Last week the company had marketed 825 million shares at $70 to $78; on Wednesday it sold more stock, and at a higher price, than that range implied. SpaceX later reached $85.7 billion after its overallotment was exercised.

Anthropic’s underwriters have the option to buy up to a further 147 million Class A shares, which would bring in another $12.2 billion and take the IPO total to $93.5 billion if exercised. They have until 20 November to take up that option. The offering itself is expected to close on 20 November, subject to customary conditions.

The banks on the deal are due about $550 million in underwriting fees, according to the company’s filing, more than the roughly $500 million paid on the SpaceX IPO.

The company priced the offering above its marketed range and increased the number of shares being sold, initially valuing the Claude developer at $1.5 trillion. Investors who received an allocation pay the $83 offering price. Anyone buying once the shares are listed pays the market price, which closed at $97.17.

Demand was unusually lopsided. Retail interest in the IPO was the largest in history. Anthropic prioritized institutional investors it already knew, and roughly half of the firms that placed orders were left empty-handed, a higher share than usual.

Retail allocation came in at around 15%, below the roughly 20% the company had targeted, though still above the 5% to 10% typical in most IPOs.

Analysts who opened coverage stayed above the close. Melius started at Buy with a $155 price target; Ben Reitzes, the firm’s head of technology research, said that assigned value could even be “conservative”. Needham’s Scott Berg has a Buy rating and a $150 target. The average target across five Buy ratings was about $116.

Wolfe Research, in a Thursday note, said cybersecurity could match Anthropic’s coding opportunity and reach $500 billion annually.

The company has given a sense of the scale behind that interest. In its prospectus, Anthropic said it generated $33.24 billion of revenue in the nine months to 30 September, up about 1,200% from the same period a year earlier, and that its run-rate revenue was about $81 billion by the end of October.

What comes next is tightly timetabled. Index funds will not add the stock immediately. The Morningstar US Total Market Index will include it after five trading days, the Nasdaq-100 after 18 December, and the S&P 500 will not add it for at least a year.

About 15.5 billion insider shares are subject to lock-up agreements that run until after Anthropic reports results in the third quarter of next year. No date has been set for the first earnings report.

The official terms of the offering are in our report on Anthropic’s official IPO pricing. The first print is covered in our report on how ANT opened.

The wider timetable is on our Anthropic IPO date, valuation and ticker hub. For access and why the open-market price is not $83, see how to buy Anthropic stock.

data.title: XRP price trapped below $1 as bears take control: is another crash coming?
data.description:
XRP extended its losses on Friday as persistent selling pressure and weakening derivatives indicators continued to weigh on the coin.

Market data suggests that traders remain cautious about the possibility of a sustained recovery, with negative funding rates and sell-side dominance reinforcing the bearish outlook.

According to CoinGlass, XRP's long-to-short ratio has fallen near its lowest level in more than a month.

Meanwhile, CryptoQuant data shows continued selling activity across spot and futures markets, including large whale orders that could contribute to further volatility.

XRP trades around $0.963, struggling to reclaim the psychological $1 level as its major moving averages continue to signal a broader downtrend.

XRP funding rates signal bearish market sentiment

Derivatives data suggests that bearish sentiment remains prominent across the XRP market. According to CoinGlass, XRP's funding rate stood at -0.0025% on Friday.

Negative funding rates indicate that traders holding short positions are paying those holding long positions in perpetual futures markets.

XRP's long-to-short ratio declined to 0.96, approaching its lowest reading in more than a month.

A ratio below 1 indicates that short positions outnumber long positions under the metric's methodology, highlighting the prevailing bearish sentiment.

The combination of negative funding rates and long-to-short ratios suggests that XRP remains vulnerable to volatility.

On-chain and trading activity indicators provide further evidence of cautious market sentiment.

According to CryptoQuant, XRP's spot and futures markets continue to show sell-side dominance, suggesting that aggressive selling activity remains stronger than buying demand.

The platform also identifies large whale orders and elevated market activity, described as heating conditions. These indicators suggest that major market participants remain active even as XRP struggles to recover.

For XRP, the combination of elevated activity and sell-side dominance reinforces concerns about continued downward pressure.

XRP struggles below $1 as moving averages remain bearish

XRP's technical outlook continues to favor sellers as the cryptocurrency trades below its major daily Exponential Moving Averages (EMAs).

At approximately $0.962, XRP remains below the 50-day EMA at $1.198, the 100-day EMA at $1.250, and the 200-day EMA at $1.324.

These indicators represent important resistance levels that could limit potential recovery attempts.

Trading below all three indicators suggests that bearish momentum remains dominant across multiple timeframes.

Meanwhile, the Relative Strength Index (RSI) stands near 29, placing XRP within the oversold territory.

The Moving Average Convergence Divergence (MACD) indicator also remains negative, although its weakening downside momentum suggests that selling pressure may be moderating.

This combination leaves room for a short-term recovery, but the broader technical structure remains bearish. XRP faces several resistance levels as buyers attempt to stabilize prices.

The first major obstacle stands at the psychological $1 level. A sustained recovery above this threshold could improve short-term sentiment and encourage buyers to target the next resistance near $1.160.

Beyond this level, the 50-day EMA at $1.198 represents another significant barrier. Reclaiming the 50-day EMA would provide an early indication that the bearish trend is beginning to weaken.

However, XRP would still face resistance at the 100-day EMA near $1.250 and the horizontal barrier around $1.300. Further resistance stands at the 200-day EMA near $1.324, followed by higher levels at $1.540 and $1.900.

On the downside, the available technical analysis does not identify a clearly established nearby support level. This increases uncertainty about where buyers might intervene if selling pressure intensifies.

For now, XRP would need to reclaim several resistance levels before the broader technical outlook could turn more constructive.

data.title: New Zealand's FMA tightens CFD leverage and suitability rules for retail traders
data.description:
New Zealand's Financial Markets Authority (FMA) has tightened the licence conditions for firms that issue derivatives to retail investors, introducing leverage limits and stricter suitability checks for products such as contracts for difference (CFDs) and margin forex.

The regulator announced the changes on 17 November. They take effect on 18 November 2027, giving licensed derivatives issuers a year to adjust their onboarding and margin systems.

"Derivatives can be useful financial products, but they can also expose investors to significant risks, particularly where leverage is involved," said FMA general counsel Liam Mason.

Suitability checks with teeth

The first change is to the existing suitability condition. From November 2027, issuers must gather enough information to assess whether a product is suitable for a retail investor before allowing them to trade it, and must not permit trading where a product is unsuitable or not understood, the FMA said.

According to a legal update from law firm MinterEllison, the test moves from whether an investor "has the ability to understand" a derivative to whether the issuer has taken all reasonable steps to "determine whether the retail investor understands" its risks.

The revised condition also removes the current discretion to go ahead with a trade after issuing a written warning to a client who has not supplied enough information, MinterEllison said. Firms will also have to keep records of their suitability assessments.

MinterEllison noted that an FMA sector risk assessment in December 2020 found a quarter of the derivatives issuers licensed at the time were not taking reasonable steps to make suitability assessments.

Leverage limits, with an opt-out

The second change is a new leverage condition. New Zealand has not previously imposed leverage limits on derivatives issuers.

Under the condition published by the FMA, over-the-counter derivatives offered to retail investors must require a minimum initial margin of:

  • 3.33% for major currency pairs;
  • 5% for minor currency pairs, major stock market indices and gold;
  • 10% for minor indices and commodities other than gold;
  • 20% for other underlyings;
  • 50% for cryptoassets.

That equates to maximum leverage of 30:1 on major currency pairs, falling to 2:1 on crypto. Issuers subject to the condition would also have to close out positions when a client's account equity falls below the required maintenance margin.

The condition is not a blanket cap, however. Firms can keep offering higher leverage if they have three protections in place: negative balance protection, which limits a firm's recourse to the money and property in the client's account; a mandatory close-out when a client's margin falls below 50% of the required level; and a board-approved framework for identifying and supporting vulnerable investors.

The FMA said the additional measures are designed to reduce the risk of significant losses "while preserving access to higher-risk products where appropriate safeguards are in place".

How it compares

The margin tiers mirror the retail CFD leverage limits that the European Securities and Markets Authority introduced across the EU in 2018 and that the UK's Financial Conduct Authority also applies. In those markets, however, the caps sit alongside the 50% close-out rule and negative balance protection rather than being an alternative to them.

New Zealand's approach therefore leaves room for issuers that already run Europe-style protections to continue offering higher leverage locally, provided they add a vulnerable investor framework. Traders comparing providers can see how leverage, protections and costs differ in our guides to the best CFD brokers and best forex brokers.

The FMA said the final conditions follow consultation in 2024 and 2025 and evidence from its supervisory work, complaints, disputes and court findings, and that it refined parts of its original proposals after industry feedback.

What happens next

Licensed derivatives issuers in New Zealand now have until 18 November 2027 to update client onboarding, record-keeping and margin close-out processes, or to put the three alternative protections in place.

data.title: SpaceX stock: why are lenders trying to stop Elon Musk's AI space plans?
data.description:
SpaceX faces fresh questions over its artificial intelligence expansion after lenders backing a reported $43 billion financing package sought assurances that Elon Musk would not launch the Nvidia chips securing the debt into orbit.

The proposed restrictions, reported by the Financial Times on Friday, reflect concerns that valuable computing equipment would be difficult to recover if SpaceX defaulted. Whether the provisions entered the final agreements remains unclear.

SpaceX stock (NASDAQ: SPCX) closed 3.53% lower at $138.43 on Thursday, before the lender concerns were widely reported.

The dispute highlights a growing tension between Musk's plans for orbital data centres and the practical demands of financing AI infrastructure.

SpaceX stock: Why lenders want Nvidia chips to stay on Earth

The financing, known as Project Saturn, supports the purchase of Nvidia processors for SpaceX's expanding AI business.

Investors bought more than $30 billion of debt on Thursday, with Bloomberg reporting a roughly $32 billion bond sale.

The largest portion is a $25 billion investment-grade bond backed by approximately five years of lease payments for the GPUs.

The new securities reportedly yield about 8.3%, compared with roughly 7.2% on SpaceX debt maturing in 2031.

The structure offers lenders security in the underlying chips and contractual payments. But servers launched into orbit would be far harder to repossess, transport or sell after a default than equipment installed in a terrestrial data centre.

Rapid advances in semiconductor technology also mean their collateral value could diminish before the debt matures, heightening the importance of physical access.

"The SpaceX GPU deal appears cleverly structured," Shorecliff Asset Management chief investment officer Grant Nachman told the Financial Times, identifying potential demand from insurers seeking higher-yielding investment-grade debt.

Elon Musk's orbital data centres face an engineering test

Musk wants to place powerful computing systems aboard satellites, potentially using solar energy in orbit to support AI workloads without some of the land and electricity constraints facing Earth-based facilities.

Doing so would introduce problems conventional data centres rarely confront. Heat must be radiated into space, components must survive radiation and extreme conditions, and faulty equipment cannot readily be replaced.

Communications capacity and the cost of launch add further uncertainty.

Reusable Starship rockets could eventually make carrying substantial hardware into orbit more affordable.

SpaceX made progress in its November test programme, although the heavy-lift system has not established routine, economical reuse.

“Starship remains the enabling infrastructure” behind major opportunities, including orbital data centres and expanded Starlink deployments, KeyBanc analyst Mike Leshock told MarketWatch.

For now, SpaceX says its Apollo-backed GPU arrangement is intended for terrestrial computing.

That difference matters: financing assets in orbit may require protections fundamentally different from those supporting ordinary equipment leases.

What the financing dispute means for SpaceX stock

In October, SpaceX announced a binding commitment for an approximately $40 billion equipment lease with an Apollo-managed entity.

Deliveries of Nvidia Vera Rubin systems are expected to begin during the first half of 2027, subject to closing conditions.

The earlier lease and the reported $43 billion financing describe related arrangements, not two separate sums to be added together.

Investors remain divided on how much value to assign SpaceX's emerging AI business.

Morgan Stanley analyst Adam Jonas reiterated an Overweight rating and $300 price target, with $170 of that target attributed to enterprise AI, according to TheStreet.

"On FY28, SPCX trades cheaper than the S&P500. Interesting," Jonas wrote in an earlier valuation note.

By contrast, Morningstar estimates fair value at $70, reflecting concerns about infrastructure spending and whether AI demand can justify the investment.

data.title: Here's why gold prices are crashing 9% in their worst week in eight months
data.description:
Gold prices sank to their lowest level since September 2025 on Friday, putting bullion on course for its steepest weekly decline in eight months as investors adjusted to the prospect of further US interest-rate increases.

Spot gold fell 2.7% to $3,525.25 an ounce by 05:04 GMT, extending its weekly slide to about 9.2%. December US gold futures dropped 4.3% to $3,526.

The retreat came even as Asian technology shares faced renewed selling pressure, a reminder that gold does not always benefit from market turmoil.

Gold price today: Fed outlook strengthens the dollar's grip

The dollar remained near a 19-month high, making bullion more expensive for buyers using other currencies. Rising US Treasury yields also offered investors an income-bearing alternative to gold.

Minutes from the Federal Reserve's October meeting, published on Wednesday, showed almost all policymakers anticipated further tightening to bring inflation towards the central bank's 2% target.

Markets assigned a 96.8% probability to a quarter-percentage-point rate increase in December, against a 3.2% chance of a half-point move, according to a Friday morning CME FedWatch snapshot.

Philadelphia Fed President Anna Paulson reinforced the case for higher rates on Thursday, describing October's pause as a matter of pace rather than a change in direction.

Fawad Razaqzada, a market analyst at FOREX.com, said in research published Thursday that rising real yields were particularly damaging for gold because it pays no interest. A meaningful recovery, he argued, may require a pause in the dollar's rally.

Gold price crash: Liquidations magnify the sell-off

The decline has accelerated as some investors close positions rather than wait for bullion to recover.

Capital.com analyst Kyle Rodda attributed part of the move to forced selling across financial markets, with persistent inflation and a stronger dollar adding to the pressure.

Mauricio Di Bartolomeo, co-founder of lending company Ledn, offered a related interpretation in comments published by The Wall Street Journal.

After gold's earlier gains, some holders may be choosing to realise profits and move into US Treasuries, which now offer comparatively attractive yields.

Other precious metals also declined. Spot silver dropped 3.5% to $41.25 an ounce, platinum lost 3.6% to $1,299.25 and palladium slid 3.3% to $879.47.

Separately, Swiss customs figures showed gold exports fell 34% in October to 109.7 tonnes, driven by fewer shipments to Britain.

The data illustrate changing physical bullion flows, rather than explaining Friday's price plunge on their own.

Is $3,500 the next test for gold price?

The speed of the retreat has brought $3,500 into focus.

Razaqzada warned in an assessment covered by Kitco that gold could test that level if expectations of tighter policy keep lifting yields and supporting the dollar.

That is a conditional technical risk, not a firm price prediction.

Gold has already fallen far enough to raise the prospect of a brief oversold rebound, but Razaqzada cautioned that weak momentum still favours sellers.

Traders will now look towards the Fed's 8–9 December meeting and the November US consumer inflation report scheduled for 10 December.

A softer inflation reading or a retreat in the dollar could help stabilise gold. Until then, bullion remains exposed to further selling driven by yields, currency movements and leveraged positions.

data.title: Why did Anthropic stock lose half its opening gains on IPO day?
data.description:
Anthropic stock (NASDAQ: ANT) lost roughly half their opening premium on Thursday as the artificial intelligence developer's record-breaking Nasdaq debut ran into valuation concerns and a sharp sell-off across Wall Street.

The Claude maker opened at $111.50, or 34.3% above its $83 initial public offering price, and reached $114.99. By the close, shares had retreated to $97.17, still 17.1% above the offer price.

That left investors who bought at the opening trade facing a 12.9% decline, despite a profitable first session for those allocated shares at the IPO price.

The reversal exposed the gap between demand for an AI listing and doubts about the price investors should pay.

Anthropic stock: A record debut loses its early momentum

Anthropic raised $81.34 billion by selling 980 million shares, after increasing the offering and pricing it above the original $70 to $78 range.

The total includes shares sold by investors, meaning not all proceeds will go to the company. Anthropic has also arranged a separate $26 billion private placement involving major technology groups.

Trading began shortly before noon in New York. The opening surge briefly lifted Anthropic's fully diluted valuation above $2 trillion, against about $1.5 trillion at the offering price.

But the rush did not last. Shares lost $14.33 between the open and the close, surrendering just over half of the initial $28.50 premium above the IPO price.

"Both the jump from the offer price and the high volatility are not surprising," University of Florida professor Jay Ritter told CBS News, citing differing views of Anthropic's future profitability.

The pullback is consistent with investors reassessing what to pay after an unusually strong opening, although individual sellers' motives cannot be established from trading data alone.

Anthropic IPO news: A $2 trillion valuation meets costly ambitions

Anthropic's business is expanding at a remarkable pace. Revenue reached $33.2 billion in the first nine months of 2026, up more than twelvefold from a year earlier.

Even so, the company recorded an operating loss of about $1.3 billion. It also disclosed $900.9 billion in purchase and lease commitments, mainly tied to computing infrastructure, extending over multiple years.

Some $451.6 billion of those commitments is expected before the end of 2030. The figure is not an immediate cash bill, but underscores the investment required to keep developing and serving sophisticated AI models.

At Thursday's opening price, the company's valuation approached $2 trillion. By the close, it had fallen to approximately $1.76 trillion on a fully diluted basis.

"We got in at a far lower valuation through the private markets," Strategy Asset Managers chief executive Tom Hulick told Investing.com, explaining why his firm was not adding at the debut price.

His stance illustrates the difference between believing in Anthropic's growth and finding its shares attractive at any price.

The wider AI sell-off makes investors cautious

Anthropic's debut did not reverse weakness elsewhere in technology stocks. The Nasdaq Composite fell 2.25% on Thursday, while the S&P 500 lost 2.02%.

Nvidia declined 3.3% and Advanced Micro Devices shed 7.7%, amid worries about AI spending, financing costs and richly valued technology businesses.

"Don't mistake one blockbuster deal for an all-clear signal," technology analyst Luke Lango warned in The Wall Street Journal.

Some investors are reassessing the cost of financing AI infrastructure as US interest-rate expectations rise. Higher borrowing costs can pressure richly valued growth shares, especially when profits depend on spending years ahead.

Competition from OpenAI, Google and lower-cost models adds another reason for investors to demand evidence of returns.
